rv.q: Nothing about the production is particularly interesting or innovative. It’s a standard bio-musical...Everything is just so perfect and glossy, from the choreography to the beautiful costumes to the huge group of performers at the top of their, or anyone else’s, game.
This musical never fully sparks into life...Simply the best? Not quite.
Warren's knockdown performance here not only elevates an otherwise routine bio-musical into a triumph, it's a slam-dunk for every upcoming awards ceremony.
It's everything you expected, executed well and packs in a few surprises.

This is a unique jukebox musical that isn't scared to delve into difficult themes including racism and spousal abuse to highlight Turner's tough journey to stardom and her extraordinary courage and drive to succeed.
Tina: The Tina Turner Musical is an ambitious musical tackling more than you might expect from a show of this genre.
It’s good to have the show back.

Tina is mostly a high-voltage showcase for Warren, who is rarely offstage and constantly in motion for almost the entirety of this two-hours-plus production. Petite and slender, the 31-year-old Virginia native lacks Turner's warrior-queen physique and earthy, sweat-soaked, thunderdome roar.
The problem for me is that, at least for the first act which charts her relationship with Ike, what we actually witness is a strong woman being brought down by multiple acts of violence.
